Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:10:1.hebrew: וה"מ דלית בהו נקבה - דהתם משום נקבה הוא דעבדי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:10:1.english: And these matters [apply] where there is no female among them - For there [when a female is present], it is because of the female that they do [so].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:13:1.hebrew: דשוויא לתרוייכו - אגדתא ושמעתתא בדבר אחד, ושניכם שוין בה, שתתרצו ותחפצו בה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:13:1.english: That is fitting for both of you - Aggadah and halakhic teaching in one matter, and both of you are equal in it, [in] that you will be pleased with it and desire it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:13:2.hebrew: כי תצא מעצמה - אנחנו גרמנו לו שקלקלנו, והבטיח הקב"ה לשלם כאילו הוא הבעירה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:13:2.english: If [a fire] breaks out by itself - We caused [it] to Him, for we acted corruptly, and the Holy One, Blessed be He, promised to pay as though He had kindled it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:15:1.hebrew: פתח הכתוב בנזקי - שהזיק ממונו, דכתיב "כי תצא", משמע מעצמה — שהדליק בתוך שלו והלכה ודלקה בתוך של חבירו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:15:1.english: The verse begins with damage [of] - [meaning] that his property caused damage, as it is written, "When [a fire] goes out," [which] implies [it went out] on its own — that he kindled [a fire] within his own [property], and it went and burned within his fellow's [property].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:15:2.english: And concludes with damage [caused by] his body - For [Scripture] called him "one who kindles" with [his own] hands.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:15:3.hebrew: משום חציו - כזורק חץ שמזיק למרחוק, דאיהו גופיה עביד; הכא נמי איהו גופיה עביד. ונפקא מיניה לחייבו בד' דברים אם הוזק בה אדם, כדאמרינן בפ"ב (דף כג.):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:15:3.english: Due to his arrows - [It is] like one who shoots an arrow that causes damage from afar, where he himself performs [the action]; here too, he himself performs [the action]. And the practical difference [from this] is to obligate him for the four [additional] payments if a person was injured by it, as we say in the second chapter (23a).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:16:1.english: Which is by the gate - [The] Sanhedrin, the elders of the gate.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:17:1.hebrew: טמון באש קמיבעיא ליה - מעשה בא לפניו במחנה ששרפו אנשיו גדיש של ישראל, ונצרך לשאול הלכה, אם חייבין לשלם כלים הטמונים בתוכו כר' יהודה, או פטורין כרבנן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:17:1.english: He was asking about a concealed [article] in a fire - A case came before him in the camp, where his men burned a stack of grain belonging to an Israelite, and he needed to ask the halakha: whether they are liable to pay for vessels concealed inside it, in accordance with Rabbi Yehudah, or exempt, in accordance with the Rabbis.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:18:1.hebrew: גדישין דשעורין הוו - אקרא סמיך, דכתיב "ותהי חלקת השדה מלאה שעורין":
Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:18:1.english: They were stacks of barley - He relies on the verse, as it is written: "And the plot of ground was full of barley."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:19:1.hebrew: מלך פורץ - גדר שדה אחרים לעשות לו דרך ולאוכלוסין שלו, דאמרי' בב"ב (דף ק:), דרך המלך אין לה שיעור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:19:1.english: A king may breach - [the] fence of the field of others to make a path for himself and for his troops, as we say in Bava Batra (100b): The king's road has no [prescribed] measure.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:1:1.hebrew: בכי טוב - בעוד חמה זורחת ילין במלון, ולא ימתין עד שתחשך; ולבקר לא ישכים לצאת עד שיאיר. "כי טוב" — לישנא מעליא, "האור כי טוב", כלומר: טוב הוא לצאת בו וליכנס בו מפני המזיקין והליסטין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:1:1.english: At “it is good” - While the sun is still shining, he should lodge at an inn and not wait until it grows dark; and in the morning, he should not rise early to set out until it becomes light. “It is good” is a refined expression, [alluding to] “the light, that it was good” — that is to say, it is good to go out in it and to enter in it because of harmful spirits and bandits.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:22:1.english: Full of lentils - In the Book of Samuel.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:22:2.english: Full of barley, etc. - In Chronicles.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:24:1.hebrew: ויצילה - שלא ישרפוה, הואיל ואסור להציל את עצמו בממון חבירו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:24:1.english: And saved it - So that they would not burn it, since it is forbidden to save oneself with another's property.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:2:1.english: The sword - The sword of the Angel of Death.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:2:2.hebrew: אימה - אימת מות של מלאך, ולא בגלוי כל כך:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:2:2.english: Terror - [The] fear of death from an angel [of death], and not so openly.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:3:1.hebrew: תא שמע - וסיפיה דקרא: "ועתה לכו ונפלה אל מחנה ארם, אם יחיונו נחיה וגו'":
Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:3:1.english: Come [and] hear - And the end of the verse [is]: "Now come, let us go over to the camp of Aram; if they spare us, we shall live, etc."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:4:1.hebrew: אימה - אימת מות של מלאך, ולא בגלוי כל כך:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:4:1.english: Terror - [The] terror of death from an angel, and not so much in the open.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:5:2.english: Closed the windows - [He] stopped up [the] windows.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:6:1.english: If we say, etc. - [This is said] regarding the four leprous men.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 60b:7:1.english: That there is no uncertainty of [danger to] life - In the place to which you will be exiled.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 60b:18:1.english: What is [the law regarding] saving oneself with another's property - He raised the dilemma whether he is obligated to pay when he saved himself due to danger to life.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 60b:1:1.hebrew: לעולם יכנס אדם בכי טוב - מדקדק ר"ת מדמקדים כניסה ליציאה, דבנכנס מעיר אחרת איירי, מדיליף בריש פסחים (דף ד. ושם) מאברהם דמצפרא סגי לזרוז מצות, דכתיב: "וישכם אברהם בבקר", ודלמא משום "כי טוב" הוא דלא השכים? אלא ודאי מביתו לא שייך למימר שיצא ב"כי טוב", שמכיר המוקשים והפחתים. ואע"ג דהכא מייתי קרא: "ואתם לא תצאו איש מפתח ביתו עד בקר", משמע דמביתו נמי מיירי — יש לומר דכיון דהוא סכנתא, חשיב כמו לעיר אחרת; ובפ"ק דתענית (דף י:) מייתי קרא ד"הבקר אור". ור"י אומר דאין לדקדק בזה, דאורחיה דגמרא בהכי: בפרק במה מדליקין (שבת דף לד:): "בין השמשות כהרף עין, זה נכנס וזה יוצא"; ובפרק עושין פסין (עירובין דף כא.) נמי אמרינן: "אבל אדם מטפס ועולה, מטפס ויורד". והא דיליף מ"וישכם אברהם בבקר" — שפיר יליף, דמשום "כי טוב" לא היה צריך לאחר, כיון דאזל לדבר מצוה, דשלוחי מצוה אין נזוקין:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 60b:1:1.english: A person should always enter at "ki tov" - Rabbeinu Tam infers from the fact that [the Gemara] places entering before leaving that it is speaking of one who enters from another city, [and also] from the fact that [the Gemara] derives in the beginning of Pesachim (4a and there) from Abraham that [starting] in the morning suffices for [the principle of] "the zealous hasten to perform mitzvot," as it is written: "And Abraham rose early in the morning" (Genesis 22:3) — and perhaps it was because of "ki tov" that he did not rise earlier [while it was still night]? Rather, certainly when [leaving] from one's own house it is not applicable to say that one must leave at "ki tov," for one is familiar with the snares and pits [around his own home]. And even though here [the Gemara] cites the verse: "And none of you shall go out of the opening of his house until the morning" (Exodus 12:22), [which] implies that it is speaking of [leaving] from one's own house as well — one can say that since it was [a time of] danger, it is considered like [going to] another city; and in the first chapter of Ta'anit (10b), [the Gemara] cites the verse: "The morning was light" (Genesis 44:3). And Ri says that one need not make an inference from this, for such is the way of the Gemara: in Perek Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 34b) [it says]: "Twilight is like the blink of an eye, this one enters and this one leaves"; and in Perek Osin Pasin (Eruvin 21a) we also say: "But a person climbs and goes up, climbs and goes down." And as for what [the Gemara] derives from "And Abraham rose early in the morning" — it derives it well, for on account of "ki tov" he would not have needed to delay, since he was going for a mitzvah matter, as those sent on a mitzvah are not harmed.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 60b:25:1.hebrew: דלא שביק להו לאחלופי - בתרוייהו כתיב "ויצילה": של שעורים — שלא נטלוה ע"מ לשלם עדשים, ושל עדשים — שלא לקחוה ממי שזכה בה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 60b:25:1.english: "That he did not permit them to exchange" - In both [verses] it is written "and he saved it" (vayatzilah): [the plot] of barley — that they did not take it with the intent to pay [with] lentils, and [the plot] of lentils — that they did not take it from the one who had acquired it.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 60b:9:1.hebrew: שמלאך המות מפקיד שם כליו - לא גרסינן "שנאמר למכמש יפקיד כליו", דגבי עשרה מסעות של סנחריב כתיב האי קרא (בישעיהו י): "בא על עית, עבר במגרון, למכמש יפקיד כליו":
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 60b:9:1.english: As the Angel of Death deposits his implements there - We do not read [in the Gemara text] "as it is stated: 'At Michmash he deposits his implements,'" for this verse is written regarding the ten journeys of Sennacherib (Isaiah 10[:28]): "He has come upon Aiath, he has passed through Migron; at Michmash he deposits his implements."
